claim_boundary: Executed bounded symbolic proxy. The three parts name verification architectures, not actual ASI systems or an Aristotle run.

parts.contract: Construct and exhaustively verify both finite mathematical presentations, then apply a strong ordinary isomorphism baseline which accepts noncanonical and orientation-reversing maps.

Assume and audit each local equality geometry before comparison, admit a raw candidate only through preservation and reflection, and retain the explicit (T, phi, pi) lineage through W/E/J/C, operation, quotient-question, and next-basis derivations.

Reveal and locally audit a separately committed external axiom-geometry packet, then test exact GeomEquiv interactions and typed non-bijective extension/quotient interactions without revising an earlier frame, question, or receipt.

freeze_order: protocol, total questions, and separate registered geometry/candidate packet hashes committed
classical local presentations and strong baseline frozen
closure-native frames, candidates, and derivations frozen
external geometry packet checked and consumed
each external geometry instantiated and audited in its own declared equality
external candidate packet checked and consumed
adjacent and composite relational certificates frozen

continuous_relational_identification.meaning: A gap-free, content-addressed, compositionally coherent finite relation history across distinct frozen isolations; not analytic or topological continuity.
required_evidence: a typed adjacent relation or explicit obstruction at every step
preservation and reflection for every exact GeomEquiv
declared image or quotient equality law for non-bijective steps
W/E/J/C and operation checks on every admitted domain
total source and target relational coverage
occurrence-level lineages and a receipt-linked returned basis

openness_rule: OpenIn is emitted only for a precommitted total question with an explicit pair x~y and Q(x)!=Q(y). Missing, partial, rejected, or obstructed interaction data are never OpenIn.
token_rule: At most one admission token belongs to the selected native returned relation. The three parts and external continuation do not mint additional tokens.
falsification: An equality, question, or earlier receipt is changed after an external interaction is revealed.
An external geometry is silently normalized to a preferred classical frame.
An exact interaction checks preservation but not reflection.
Adjacent relations pass while their declared composite disagrees with direct recomputation.
A target isolation residue is silently dropped.
A failed or partial interaction is reported as OpenIn.
The classical baseline recovers the same complete longitudinal evidence at equal or lower cost on richer paired studies.
